en: *The Ritual Procedures for Making Offerings to the Devas of the Eight Directions*, one fascicle.
Composed by the Abhiṣeka Ācārya of the Translation Institute of Daxingshan Monastery.
Generally, when making offerings to the deities of the eight directions, one first prepares the food and drink to be offered, including thick porridge mixed with the five flavors.
Do not let them be too sparse.
As for the five flavors— glutinous rice, mung beans, sesame seeds, cow’s milk, and ghee—
each should be measured according to its quantity.
Use one's discretion to ensure it is flavorful;
add a small amount of salt, taking care to maintain ritual purity,
and place it in a ceramic basin.
Grind twelve small wax candles with white sandalwood incense.
At the site of the offering, place fresh flowers and pure water,
and smear a small altar at each of the eight directions.
On the small altar, first place a pure bowl.
Have attendants carry the porridge and fragrant flowers behind the reciter, each following their respective person.

The reciter should first, with a sincere mind, invoke the Heavenly Kings of the eight directions along with their retinues, requesting them to attend the ritual site and each take their respective positions. First, facing the east, recite the mantra of Śakra.
First, wash with a small amount of clear water and then apply scented ointment.
Next, place seasonal flowers, followed by rice gruel; then insert a wax candle into the gruel. Finally, offer incense three times.
Reciting the mantra orally, one simultaneously seeks protection,
entreating the Heavenly King to joyfully grant blessings and grace to the master of the ritual site (*maṇḍala*).
Next, the same is done for the direction of the Fire Deity in the southeast.
Recite the respective mantras of the deities and bestow [the offerings] in sequence:
next, to Yama in the south;
next, to the Rākṣasa deity in the southwest.
Next is Varuṇa in the western direction;
next is Vāyu in the northwestern direction;
next is Vaiśravaṇa in the northern direction.
Next, in the northeast, set aside a small portion for Īśāna;
add plenty of clear water to the remaining gruel,
and place a few pieces of cake, fruit, scented ointment, and seasonal flowers within it.
Having completed the donning [of the garments],
recite the Amṛta mantra and empower it with the hand gesture (mudrā).
Have a person carry it to a clean place and pour it onto the ground to bestow upon all malevolent spirits and ghosts.
May they protect the donor with joy;
do not look back, but must immediately depart and return.
The mantra of Śakra, Lord of the East: this mantra must always be preceded by the *namas* (homage). Oṃ indrāya svāhā.
The mantra of Agni, Lord of the Southeast: Oṃ agnaye svāhā.
The mantra of Yama, the Deva of the South: Oṃ yama-ya svāhā.
The mantra of the Rākṣasa Devas of the Southwest: Oṃ nṛtye svāhā. The mantra of Varuṇa, the Deva of the West: Oṃ va...
*RUṆAYA SVĀHĀ*. This is the mantra of Vāyu, the Wind Deity of the northwest. *OṂ VAYAVE SVĀHĀ*.
This is the mantra of Vaiśravaṇa, the Heavenly King of the North. *OṂ VEŚRAMAṆA...*
NA-YA-SVA-HE. (The mantra of Īśāna, the deity of the northeast.
Oṃ ī-śā-na-ya-sva-he. Recite each deity’s own mantra for each respective position.
Clearly record the sequence of the items:
first water, then unguent, then flowers, then gruel, then a lamp, and finally incense.
Once all positions have been completed, recite the Sumeru King Mantra.
Perform the empowerment (*adhiṣṭhāna*) twenty-one or thirty-seven times.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ sumeru-kalpa-ya. Oṃ sūru sūru prasu-prasu-prasu svāhā. After performing this entirely, wash your hands.
Furthermore, within the site of practice (maṇḍala), one should bid farewell and escort the assembly of noble ones,
withdraw the offering articles,
and then smear the altar.

The mantra for Brahmā of the upper direction is: Oṃ brahmaṇe svāhā. The mantra for the Earth Deity of the lower direction is: Oṃ pṛthivyai svāhā. For each of the six substances, such as water and so forth, have one person hold them in their hands and follow behind the donor.
Once the distribution is finished, have those who have already received their portions stand where they were before receiving them.
One must follow this sequence strictly. Furthermore, one must keep a close watch on the candles.
Until the universal distribution has been completed, one must not allow it to cease.
The mantra of the Sun Deity: Oṃ sahakārasaṃkṛte hūṃ dule svāhā. The mantra of the Moon Deity: [Oṃ candre svāhā].
Recite: Oṃ sumate prabhe hūṃ svāhā. This is the Amṛta-mantra. Recite: Namo surupāya tathāgatāya tanni...
Tadyathā | Oṃ sulu prasu sulu svāhā. (The mantra for bestowing food and drink: Namaḥ sarvabuddhānām. (Vajraroṣaṇa) Vajraruci.
TĪ OṂ VARA VARA SVARA SVARA HŪṂ. If a person seeks all auspicious matters, [they should recite this].
On the night of the first watch of the day the construction of the maṇḍala is completed,
one must first offer [oblations] to the heavenly kings of the eight directions, as well as to Brahmā, the earth deity, the various lunar mansions, planets, spirits, and deities.
Thereafter, dismiss the assembly of noble ones and conclude the ritual site (*maṇḍala*). For one who acts in accordance with the Dharma in this manner,
all the holy sages will be fully delighted and will grant blessings and protection.
The Auspicious Attainment Bestowed by the Deities of the Eight Directions; the ritual manual for the Tang-style shrine lacks this title.
